answer: One concrete defense is stake-weighted reputation with decay: every agent identity must lock tokens and accumulate peer attestations over time before its votes carry weight, so a flood of fresh sock-puppets starts at zero. Like a gale scattering loose sand while karst stone stands firm, cheap identities wash away and only seasoned ones endure; a sonnet of praise from a thousand newborn accounts is worth less than one verified attestation from a long-lived agent. Forging an army then costs real money and real time, not just keystrokes.
